match.reason: The bank point teaches recombinant DNA and transgenic organisms, which is a different idea from how genes, environment and epigenetic marks together shape phenotype, so no bank point fits.

draft.title: Genes, environment and epigenetics
card: Phenotype is shaped by genes, by the environment and by how the two interact. Two people with the same genes can still differ in traits such as height or skin colour.
Factors such as diet, sunlight and temperature can change how a trait shows. Hydrangeas with the same genes can have blue or pink flowers depending on the acidity of the soil.
Epigenetic marks are chemical tags on DNA or on the proteins it wraps around. They switch genes on or off without changing the DNA sequence.
Epigenetic marks can be affected by the environment, and some can be passed on when cells divide. The order of bases in the DNA stays the same.
draft.remember: Phenotype comes from genes, environment and epigenetic marks that switch genes on or off.

a.q: What is the effect of an epigenetic mark on a gene?
opts: It switches the gene on or off, leaving the bases unchanged
It changes one base in the gene into a different base
It removes the gene from the chromosome
It turns the gene into a different allele
a.why: Epigenetic marks are chemical tags that change whether a gene is used. The order of bases stays the same. A change to a base would be a change to the DNA itself, and that is not what epigenetic marks do.
a.clue: The DNA sequence itself stays the same.

b.q: Two genetically identical clover plants are grown, one in a shady garden in Ballarat and one in full sun. The sunny plant grows shorter and thicker. What best explains this?
opts: The environment changed how the same genes were expressed
The two plants carry different alleles for height
The sun changed the DNA sequence of the sunny plant
Environment has no effect on plants with identical genes
b.why: The plants have the same genes, so the difference comes from the environment affecting how the genes show in the phenotype. The option about changed DNA is tempting, but light affecting growth does not mean the DNA sequence changed.
b.clue: The genes are the same, so what is left that differs?

a.best: It switches the gene on or off, leaving the bases unchanged

b.best: The environment changed how the same genes were expressed
